title: Major Rock Edict VII: All religious groups
excerpt: The king says members of all religious groups should be able to live throughout his realm.
html:
About this edict

This short edict values self-control and purity of mind across sects. It also warns that giving alone is insufficient without gratitude and disciplined conduct.

Original script

Roman transliteration

The text below follows the Girnar version in Hultzsch’s edition. Square brackets show restored or uncertain letters; dots mark damaged or missing text. Other surviving copies can differ.

(A) 1 Devānaṃpiyo Piyadasi rājā sarvata ichati save pāsaṃḍā vaseyu (B) save te sayamaṃ ca 2 bhava-sudhim ca ichati (C) jano tu ucāvaca-chamdo ucavaca-rago (D) te sarvaṃ va kāsaṃti eka-desaṃ vā kasa[ṃ]ti (E) 3 vip[ul]e tu pi dāne yasa nāsti sayame bhāva-sudhitā va kataṃñatā va daḍhabhati[t]ā ca nicā bāḍham

English translation

This is E. Hultzsch’s 1925 translation of the same version. Its terminology and bracketed restorations reflect that historical edition.

(A) King Devānāṁpriya Priyadarśin desires (that) all sects may reside everywhere. (B) (For) all these desire both self-control and purity of mind. (C) But men possess various desires (and) various passions. (D) Either they will fulfil the whole, or they will fulfil (only) a portion (of their duties). (E) But even one who (practises) great liberality, (but) does not possess self-control, purity of mind, gratitude, and firm devotion, is very mean.

Sources

  • E. Hultzsch, Inscriptions of Asoka (1925), Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, volume I.
  • Bibliotheca Polyglotta edition, University of Oslo (Magadhi transliteration, English translation, and inscription facsimiles).
